title: The watchdog's “waits for the owner” question: the owner's yes on a card another session brings is a future step, not a wait on the owner now; the same yes asked right here still is
note: Live case: a session answered another session's “may I roll out now?” and ended with “the permission for prod is yours, the card comes from that session”. The same ending got the mark in 7 of 8 tries and no mark in 8 of 8 tries with other wording, so the owner saw “answer?” next to a result that asked him nothing, and then the card itself. Texts are made up and neutral. ask-here and asks-now-no-card are the true branch: the yes asked in the result itself. Input = the language line + the end of the result, as the watchdog sends it (no open cards).

turns.input:
Owner's language: English.
Session auth asked whether it can update its settings on prod now. Nothing on the maps side is in the way, so I told them: now is fine, only not 03:05–04:45, when the maps night jobs run.

The permission to change prod is yours; session auth brings the card.

Owner's language: English.
Session auth checked: the update does not change anything maps calls, they stay compatible. They will say the rollout time in advance. The release itself goes on your yes; they bring the card.

Owner's language: English.
I only asked them to stay out of the maps night jobs, 03:05–04:45, and to tell me if the update changes what maps calls — then I check that the two work together.

The release to prod itself — on your yes, the card comes from that session.

Owner's language: English.
Session auth asked whether it can update its settings on prod now. Nothing on the maps side is in the way.

They won't bring a card: say yes here and I pass it on to them. Without your yes they wait.

Owner's language: English.
The maps 1.4 release is ready: staging is checked, the rollback plan is written. Roll it out to prod now? I won't start without your yes.
